{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The ferry to Skarvholm ran twice a day in summer and once in winter, and Eirik had driven it for so long that the passengers had become a kind of weather. He knew which of them would stand at the rail regardless of rain, which would sit inside with their coats buttoned to the throat, and which would ask him, every single crossing, whether the sea looked rough today. He always said it looked about the same.

The island had eighty-one residents when he started and thirty-four now. The school had closed in a year he could name if pressed. The shop kept shorter hours. Still the ferry ran, because a rule somewhere said it must, and because the county had not yet found the sentence that would end it.

He liked the last crossing best, when the light went flat and copper over the water and the only passenger was often the nurse going home. She would sit near the wheelhouse door and they would not speak much. It was enough to share the sound of the engine and the long green swell.

His daughter said he should retire. She said it kindly, the way one mentions an appointment. He had nodded and changed the subject to her children.

What he could not explain was that the island did not feel emptier to him. It felt held. Each crossing was a stitch, and as long as he kept making them the thing stayed sewn to the mainland, however loosely, however few noticed the thread."}
